title: Derived exponential bijection for simplicial projective diagrams
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and their model homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property], and combinatorial simplicial model categories, enriched projective diagrams and objectwise evaluation from [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category and let $I,D$ be small simplicial categories. Write $\mathcal A^D$ for enriched functors $D\to\mathcal A$ with enriched natural transformations and its projective model structure. Let $\mathcal B=(\mathcal A^D)^{cf}$ and $\mathcal A^{cf}$ be the full simplicial subcategories of cofibrant fibrant objects. Cartesian products of simplicial categories have paired objects, product mapping simplicial sets and componentwise composition. Enriched evaluation defines $e:\mathcal B\times D\to\mathcal A^{cf}$. All displayed categories and hom sets are contained in suitably enlarged universes.

The assignment $[g]\mapsto[e\circ(g\times1_D)]$ gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,\mathcal B)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I\times D,\mathcal A^{cf}),$$
natural under enriched restriction in $I$ and derived enriched restriction in $D$. For a set $S$ of vertex arrows of $I$, this bijection identifies the subset of classes sending every $s\in S$ to an isomorphism in $\pi_0\mathcal B$ with the subset sending every $(s,1_d)$, $s\in S$, $d\in\operatorname{Ob}D$, to an isomorphism in $\pi_0\mathcal A^{cf}$. Equivalently a vertex enriched natural transformation between projectively cofibrant fibrant $D$-diagrams is invertible in $\pi_0\mathcal B$ exactly when each object component is invertible in $\pi_0\mathcal A^{cf}$. No cofibrancy or local Kan condition is imposed on $I,D$.

source.place: Propositions A.3.4.12-A.3.4.13, printed pp.889-890. The subset clause is the objectwise weak-equivalence criterion in the projective model, used in the third bijection of the proof of Lemma A.3.5.14, printed p.896; bifibrant diagram equivalences are tested in the model homotopy category. Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], $\mathcal A^D$ is a combinatorial simplicial model category and its bifibrant diagrams have bifibrant values. Its mapping sets are enriched ends. Consequently evaluation restricts to the displayed enriched functor $e:\mathcal B\times D\to\mathcal A^{cf}$: on maps, evaluate an enriched transformation at $d$ and then apply the diagram's action on $D(d,d')$; enriched naturality makes the two orders equal. Thus the proposed evaluation has the asserted target, including when $D$ is not locally Kan.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and proof using A.3.4.12, printed pp.889–890; subset condition in the third bijection of A.3.5.14, printed p.896. Agent expansion; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Currying identifies $\mathcal A^{I\times D}$ with $(\mathcal A^D)^I$. Explicitly, send $F$ to $i\mapsto(d\mapsto F(i,d))$. On a pair of mapping simplices use the action of $F$ on $I(i,i')\times D(d,d')$; conversely compose the $I$-action with the $D$-action. These actions commute by enriched naturality, and the identity and composition equations give inverse constructions on objects and transformations. The enriched-end equations agree too: both impose naturality separately in $I$ and $D$. Under this identification, a map is a weak equivalence or a fibration in either projective model precisely when every $(i,d)$ component is one, by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Trivial fibrations therefore agree, and cofibrations agree since they are exactly the maps lifting against all trivial fibrations. The identification is consequently an isomorphism of model categories and induces a bijection on object classes modulo weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and proof using A.3.4.12, printed pp.889–890; subset condition in the third bijection of A.3.5.14, printed p.896. Agent expansion; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes] first to the coefficient model category $\mathcal A^D$ with index $I$, and then to $\mathcal A$ with index $I\times D$. Together with step 2 this gives bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,\mathcal B)\cong\pi_0((\mathcal A^D)^I)\cong\pi_0(\mathcal A^{I\times D})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I\times D,\mathcal A^{cf}).$$
The cited classification allows arbitrary small indices. Both indices are small in the original universe, while the coefficient categories fit in the enlarged universe. In particular neither cofibrancy nor local Kan mapping sets of $I,D$ have been assumed.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and proof using A.3.4.12, printed pp.889–890; subset condition in the third bijection of A.3.5.14, printed p.896. Agent expansion; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The composite in step 3 is the asserted map. Represent a class on the left by the projectively bifibrant $I$-diagram $P$ in $\mathcal A^D$ supplied by the classification [lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes]. Evaluation at $i$ takes $P$ to a bifibrant $D$-diagram by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], so $P$ is a simplicial functor $I\to\mathcal B$. Step 2's uncurried diagram $\widetilde P$ is bifibrant and satisfies $\widetilde P(i,d)=P(i)(d)$, with its action exactly $e\circ(P\times1_D)$. The two classification maps therefore send its class to the required evaluated class. This also proves well-definedness for derived classes. Products descend to $h\mathrm{sCat}$: [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies realization of a product of mapping sets with its product in k-spaces; paths and based sphere maps and their homotopies into a product are coordinate pairs. Products thus preserve weak homotopy equivalences of mapping sets, and $\pi_0(C\times D)=\pi_0C\times\pi_0D$. A quasi-inverse and unit/counit for an equivalence of ordinary categories remain such after taking a product with an identity. Hence products preserve Dwyer–Kan equivalences, justifying the displayed operation also for a general representative of $[g]$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and proof using A.3.4.12, printed pp.889–890; subset condition in the third bijection of A.3.5.14, printed p.896. Agent expansion; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For any simplicial model category $\mathcal M$, [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})$ with the infinity localization of $N(\mathcal M)$, compatibly with inclusion on bifibrant objects and with enriched mapping spaces and their compositions. The homotopy category of its bifibrant nerve is $\pi_0\mathcal M^{cf}$: its arrows are components of the stated enriched mapping spaces, and composition is induced by their enriched composition. By [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category], the induced homotopy category of that infinity localization is the ordinary localization of $\mathcal M$ at its model weak equivalences. Thus a vertex map $u$ between bifibrant objects is invertible in $\pi_0\mathcal M^{cf}$ exactly when its ordinary localization image is invertible. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] to conclude that this is equivalent to $u$ being a model weak equivalence. This uses the pending nerve-localization statement as a cited theorem; it does not use or restore its withdrawn decomposition.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and proof using A.3.4.12, printed pp.889–890; subset condition in the third bijection of A.3.5.14, printed p.896. Agent expansion; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Apply step 5 to $\mathcal M=\mathcal A^D$ and to $\mathcal M=\mathcal A$. For a vertex transformation $u:P\to Q$ between projectively bifibrant diagrams, it gives
$$[u]\text{ invertible in }\pi_0\mathcal B\iff u\in W_{\mathcal A^D}\iff (\forall d)\ u_d\in W_{\mathcal A}\iff (\forall d)\ [u_d]\text{ invertible in }\pi_0\mathcal A^{cf}.$$
The middle equivalence is exactly the objectwise weak-equivalence assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], which also ensures that all endpoints $P(d),Q(d)$ are bifibrant. Represent $[g]$ by $P$ as in step 4 and apply this criterion to the vertex transformation $P(s)$ for every $s\in S$. Its evaluated component is precisely $\widetilde P(s,1_d)$. This proves the subset assertion and its equivalent transformation formulation. Invertibility is unchanged by the natural isomorphisms induced by changing representatives, so the condition depends only on the derived class.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and proof using A.3.4.12, printed pp.889–890; subset condition in the third bijection of A.3.5.14, printed p.896. Agent expansion; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For restriction $a:I'\to I$, the formula $\widetilde{P\circ a}(i',d)=P(a(i'))(d)$ identifies evaluation after restriction with restriction along $a\times1_D$. The naturality clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes] identifies these operations on derived classes even when a projective replacement is needed. For $b:D'\to D$, restriction $b^*$ preserves objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Apply restriction to the diagrams in step 3 and then take bifibrant representatives. Since $b^*$ preserves weak equivalences, the replacement arrows give the same weak-equivalence classes as restricting before replacement. Currying commutes with this restriction by the formula $\widetilde{b^*P}(i,d')=P(i)(b(d'))$, on both objects and action maps. The naturality of classification therefore gives the claimed square with derived enriched restriction on $\mathcal B$ and restriction along $1_I\times b$ on the right. Identities and composites follow from these same pointwise formulas and the independence of replacement classes.
